readme:
# Unblinded Dataset for the Ligand Poses challenge

## 🏆 Antiviral Challenge
ASAP Discovery and Open ADMET organized [a blind challenge](https://polarishub.io/competitions/asap-discovery/antiviral-drug-discovery-2025) on Polaris in early 2025. It consisted of three parts: ADMET, Potency and Ligand Poses. **This is the unblinded dataset for the [Ligand Poses challenge](https://polarishub.io/competitions/asap-discovery/antiviral-ligand-poses-2025)**. 

- Participants were tasked with predicting the bound Ligand Pose, given the CXSMILES, Chain A Sequence, Chain B Sequence and Protein Label.
- The complete evaluation logic has been published [on Github](https://github.com/asapdiscovery/asap-polaris-blind-challenge-examples/tree/main/evaluation).
- The final leaderboard for this challenge had a total of 39 submissions, which can be found [here](https://polarishub.io/competitions/asap-discovery/antiviral-drug-discovery-2025#competiton-results).

## 📊 Data

| Column |  Dtype | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chain A Sequence | str | Primary structure of the protein's A chain: A linear sequence of amino acids. |
| Chain B Sequence | str | Primary structure of the protein's B chain, if any: A linear sequence of amino acids. |
| CXSMILES | str | Text representation of the 2D molecular structure |
| Complex Structure | PDB ([`fastpdb.AtomArray`](https://github.com/biotite-dev/fastpdb)) | 3D system of the ligand bound to the protein, prepared using OESpruce and aligned to a reference Mpro |
| Protein Structure | PDB ([`fastpdb.AtomArray`](https://github.com/biotite-dev/fastpdb)) | 3D system of just the protein structure, prepared using OESpruce and aligned to a reference Mpro |
| Ligand Pose | SDF ([`rdkit.Chem.Mol`](https://github.com/rdkit/rdkit)) | 3D conformation of the molecule, bound to the protein |
| Protein Label | str | Either `SARS-CoV-2 Mpro` or `MERS-CoV Mpro` |
| Set | Categorical | Whether this was part of the train or test set |

## ⚠️ Known Issues
We're publishing the full dataset for transparency and reproducibility, but please be aware that the dataset has some known issues that were surfaced during the challenge.

### Duplicates
The dataset included duplicates for the following three reasons: 

- Compounds showed variations in poses (n=6) so both variants were uploaded into individual entries
- Uploaded newer version or better data for a compound (n=2) so the newer variant is the one used in guiding design
- Simple duplication in uploading a second dataset (n=1)

In other words: For certain protein, ligand pairs, there were multiple possible poses. For those duplicates, we evaluated the best pose with the minimal RMSD for the challenge. See the code [here](https://github.com/asapdiscovery/asap-polaris-blind-challenge-examples/blob/main/evaluation/ligand_poses.py#L52-L63).

Set.description: Whether this molecule was part of the train or test set in the original competition

CXSMILES.description: Text representation of the 2D molecular structure of the ligand

Ligand Pose.description: 3D conformation of the ligand in its binding pose

Chain A Sequence.description: Primary structure of the A chain of the protein: A linear sequence of amino acids.

Chain B Sequence.description: Primary structure of the B chain of the protein: A linear sequence of amino acids.

Complex Structure.description: 3D system of the ligand bound to the protein

Protein Structure.description: 3D system of just the protein structure, prepared using OESpruce and aligned to a reference Mpro
